fullPassage:
Every language has its distinctive expressions, but some places have truly unique and culturally rich idioms and sayings. Ready to explore some of the most unique idioms from around the world? Join us on a journey to discover them!
When your German friend says "Have a pig!" to you, it's a way of wishing you good luck. The saying dates back to medieval times when farmers who could raise many pigs were considered prosperous. Therefore, as New Year's Eve approaches, people in Germany give each other candies in a pig shape as a way to wish each other good luck in the coming year.
In Thailand, when people say "You're riding an elephant to catch a grasshopper," they mean that you're putting in a tremendous amount of effort for a very small reward. It's quite simple to understand. Imagine trying to catch a tiny grasshopper by riding a massive elephant — it's a huge effort for a tiny result.
In Portugal, there's a saying: "Don't feed the donkey sponge cake." This expression emphasizes the idea of not giving valuable things to those who don't appreciate or deserve them. It's pretty simple — donkeys are perfectly happy with carrots and sugar, so there's no need to give them your sponge cake!
In Finland, if you say the wrong thing, you're "letting a frog out of your mouth"! That makes sense since spitting a frog at someone is generally a bad idea. Finland is considered one of the greenest countries on earth, so it should be no surprise that the Finns enjoy nature idioms.

det.korean: 모든 언어에는 독특한 표현이 있다. 이 표현은 중세 시대로 거슬러 올라간다. 돼지를 많이 기를 수 있는 농부는 풍요로운 것으로 여겨졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① distinctive — medieval — prosperous
❌ ② destructive — medieval — dangerous
❌ ③ distinctive — modern — dangerous
❌ ④ destructive — modern — prosperous
✅ (A) distinctive: '독특한' 표현. destructive(파괴적인)는 맥락 반대. ✅ (B) medieval: 중세 시대. modern(현대)은 반대. ✅ (C) prosperous: 돼지를 많이 기르면 '번영한'. dangerous(위험한)는 무관.
det.tip: distinctive: 독특한. medieval: 중세의. prosperous: 번영하는, 풍요로운.

det.korean: 매우 작은 보상을 위해 엄청난 노력을 쏟는다. 거대한 코끼리를 타고 메뚜기를 잡는다. 이 표현은 가치 있는 것을 감사하지 않는 이에게 주지 말라는 생각을 강조한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① tremendous — massive — emphasizes
❌ ② minimum — massive — ignores
❌ ③ tremendous — miniature — ignores
❌ ④ minimum — miniature — emphasizes
✅ (A) tremendous: '엄청난' 노력. minimum(최소한의)은 반대. ✅ (B) massive: '거대한' 코끼리. miniature(축소형)는 반대. ✅ (C) emphasizes: 핵심 생각을 '강조'. ignores(무시)는 반대.
det.tip: tremendous: 엄청난, 막대한. massive: 거대한. emphasize: 강조하다.

questions.passage: It's quite simple to understand. Imagine trying to catch a tiny grasshopper by riding a massive elephant — it's a huge effort for a tiny result. det.analysis:
✅ ① valuable — appreciate — greenest
❌ ② useless — appreciate — driest
❌ ③ valuable — create — driest
❌ ④ useless — create — greenest
✅ (A) valuable: 스펀지 케이크 = '가치 있는' 것. useless(쓸모없는)는 맥락 반대. ✅ (B) appreciate: '감사하다/가치를 알다'. create(만들다)는 무관. ✅ (C) greenest: 핀란드 = 가장 '녹색인' 나라. driest(가장 건조한)는 반대.
det.tip: valuable: 가치 있는. appreciate: 감사하다, 진가를 알다. greenest: 가장 친환경적인.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 캔디를 줘서 행운(good luck)을 빈다. bad luck(불운)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①good luck: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②prosperous: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③approaches: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④bad luck: 원문은 good luck. 행운을 비는 것이 맥락.
det.tip: good luck(행운) ↔ bad luck(불운). 캔디를 주는 것은 행운을 비는 행위.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 매우 작은(small) 보상. large(큰)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①tremendous: 원문 그대로. ❌ ②large: 원문은 small. 코끼리로 메뚜기 잡기 = 큰 노력, 작은 보상. ✅ ③tiny: 원문 그대로. ✅ ④tiny: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: small reward(작은 보상) ↔ large reward(큰 보상). 핵심: 큰 노력 vs 작은 보상의 대비.

det.tip: no need(필요 없다) vs no reason(이유 없다). 맥락상 '필요성 부재'가 핵심.

Every language has its distinctive expressions, but some places have truly unique and culturally rich idioms and sayings. Ready to explore some of the most unique idioms from around the world? Join us on a journey to discover them!
When your German friend says "Have a pig!" to you, it's a way of wishing you good luck. The saying <u>dates</u> back to medieval times when farmers who could raise many pigs were considered prosperous. Therefore, as New Year's Eve approaches, people in Germany give each other candies in a pig shape as a way to wish each other good luck in the coming year.
In Thailand, when people say "You're riding an elephant to catch a grasshopper," they mean that you're putting in a tremendous amount of effort for a very small reward. It's quite simple to understand. Imagine trying to catch a tiny grasshopper by riding a massive elephant — it's a huge effort for a tiny result.
In Portugal, there's a saying: "Don't feed the donkey sponge cake." This expression emphasizes the idea of not giving valuable things to those who don't appreciate or <u>deserve</u> them. It's pretty simple — donkeys are perfectly happy with carrots and sugar, so there's no need to give them your sponge cake!
In Finland, if you say the wrong thing, you're "letting a frog out of your mouth"! That makes sense since spitting a frog at someone is generally a bad idea. Finland is considered one of the greenest countries on earth, so it should be no surprise that the Finns enjoy nature idioms.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)의 'dates'와 (B)의 'deserve'의 의미를 가장 잘 나타낸 것은?

det.korean: (A) 이 표현은 중세 시대로 거슬러 올라간다. (B) 가치를 모르거나 자격이 없는 이에게 주지 마라.
det.analysis: ✅ ② (A)dates back=거슬러 올라가다: 시간적 기원. (B)deserve=자격이 있다: 받을 만하다. ❌ ① (B)원하다: desire와 혼동. ❌ ③④: 둘 다 뜻 불일치.
det.tip: date back to: ~로 거슬러 올라가다. deserve: ~할 자격이 있다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"successful in material terms; flourishing financially"

det.korean: "물질적으로 성공한; 재정적으로 번창하는"
det.analysis: ✅ ③prosperous: 번영하는, 부유한. 정의와 정확히 일치. ❌ ①generous(관대한): 다른 뜻. ❌ ②popular(인기 있는): 다른 뜻. ❌ ④ambitious(야심 찬): 다른 뜻.
det.tip: prosperous: 번영하는. 돼지를 많이 기르는 농부 = prosperous farmer.

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (영어로)

The museum has a large collection of __________ (culture) artifacts from ancient civilizations.

det.korean: 그 박물관은 고대 문명의 문화적 유물을 많이 소장하고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ cultural: __________ + artifacts(명사) → 형용사 필요. culture(명사) → cultural(형용사).
det.tip: culture(명사: 문화) → cultural(형용사: 문화적인). culturally(부사: 문화적으로).

questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (영어로)

She showed great __________ (appreciate) for the help she received from her colleagues.

det.korean: 그녀는 동료들로부터 받은 도움에 큰 감사를 표했다.
det.analysis: ✅ appreciation: great + __________ → 명사 필요. appreciate(동사) → appreciation(명사).
det.tip: appreciate(동사: 감사하다) → appreciation(명사: 감사). show appreciation for: ~에 감사를 표하다.
